$comment: The known weaknesses and their real fixes (constitution XI). The one source for the README table (scripts/render-weaknesses.mjs) and the About screen (T090, T103). Edit here, then run: node scripts/render-weaknesses.mjs

weaknesses.what: Devnet with a mock SKR mint
weaknesses.why: Hackathon build; no real value at stake
weaknesses.fix: Mainnet with real SKR

weaknesses.what: "Stake back" is true in SKR, not in dollars
weaknesses.why: Everything is SKR-denominated with no oracle in the contract
weaknesses.fix: A known property of SKR-native staking, stated in the app

weaknesses.what: `ladder_gate_enabled = false` — both leagues open from first launch
weaknesses.why: Nobody should have to spend a week before reaching the 21-day league; the unlock is still computed and recorded
weaknesses.fix: Flip the flag

weaknesses.what: `genesis_gate_enabled = false`
weaknesses.why: Testers have no Seeker
weaknesses.fix: Flip the flag on mainnet

weaknesses.what: Non-default `day_seconds` for test cohorts — including **one short test cohort on devnet**, from which the walkthrough and the demo video are recorded
weaknesses.why: Lets a full 7-day cycle run in 70 minutes — 10-minute days (H32) — during testing
weaknesses.fix: Admin-guarded; real cohorts always use 24 hours

weaknesses.what: A completed day's proof is client-signed
weaknesses.why: No backend in the build
weaknesses.fix: Server-side attestation signer with pinned traces

weaknesses.what: Reps banked during the day (in blocks of 10), and a completed day waiting for network, live only on the phone
weaknesses.why: No wallet prompt mid-workout; a lost phone loses that day's partial progress, and a rooted phone could edit it. A day finished offline counts only if it reaches the network before the deadline
weaknesses.fix: Covered by the attestation fix; cross-device progress later

weaknesses.what: Head-on, sagging hips are not detected; knee push-ups are counted in the Daily 25 by design
weaknesses.why: The Daily 25 accepts the phone head-on or at 45° and **counts push-ups from the knees on purpose** — a free habit for building strength. Staked Holdouts accept 45° only and refuse knee push-ups. Head-on the legs and hips point into the lens: on the phone, knee angle, knee and ankle height, hip height, torso angle and body line all read the same for knee push-ups as for honest ones (`fixtures/rep-traces/front-knees-01`), so knees could not be judged there anyway
weaknesses.fix: Money is only ever staked at 45°. A lower-body classifier would be needed to judge knees head-on

weaknesses.what: At 45° the body line is checked only coarsely, and the knee rule is 'off the floor'
weaknesses.why: Recorded on the phone, honest planks read 152–167° at 45°, so the ±10° body-line rule cannot be measured there; a rep is refused only when its median body line folds below 140°. In staked sittings, knees are judged on the push back up, mainly by how high the knee and ankle stand above the hands (honest 0.44–0.65 arm-lengths, knees down 0.32–0.39, line at 0.41), with the knee angle (below 90°: a deep kneel, or the feet raised behind) as a second signal — a leg bent in the air is allowed. All of it is one person's recordings, with the phone at floor level; the margins are 0.03–0.05. Knee push-ups filmed at a flatter angle, nearer head-on, read like honest reps
weaknesses.fix: More recorded sets, especially 45° knee push-ups recorded on the phone; a lower-body classifier if the angle proves too loose

weaknesses.what: Loose trousers hide the knees from the pose model
weaknesses.why: In loose trousers the model cannot find the knee and puts it on the ankle, so nothing about the knee can be judged: a staked sitting does not start, and says so ("Can't see knees"). Measured on one person in loose white trousers — the knee unreadable in 60–67 % of frames, against 0–1 % for fitted clothing
weaknesses.fix: Wear something fitted or roll the trousers up; the knee-on-the-floor image classifier would not depend on the knee landmark

weaknesses.what: A cobra is refused at 45°, not proven head-on
weaknesses.why: Lying flat and pressing only the chest up, hips on the floor, counted at 45° until the body line was judged on the push back up (honest 157–174°, cobra 120–134°). A cobra done with the body nearly straight, and a rep pushed up from lying on the floor, passed that check; they are refused by how far the hips have risen half-way up the push against the shoulders (honest 0.92–1.06, those 0.63–0.87, line 0.90) — with a margin of 0.02–0.03, measured on two people. From further in front than about 35° that check does not hold, so a staked sitting does not start there. Head-on no cobra has been recorded
weaknesses.fix: Record head-on cobra reps before relying on the Daily 25 there

weaknesses.what: No liveness check and no audio anti-spoofing in rep verification
weaknesses.why: The palm-liveness check was dropped on 22 September after the first sitting on real hardware: by the time the checks pass the member is face-down on the floor, and it asked them to lift a hand off it. Holding the top of a push-up starts the sitting instead — a readiness check, not a liveness one. So nothing here tells a live person from a video played to the lens, or one member from another. Microphone permission, which would, adds first-run friction and protects no real value on devnet
weaknesses.fix: Reinstate the audio check and the audio rep condition together — one move restores liveness and anti-spoofing both

weaknesses.what: Stake chips (≈ $10 / $25 / $50 / $100) are priced in SKR by the Operator from an off-chain rate — once at launch, re-checked weekly in Phase 2
weaknesses.why: The contract must never read a price
weaknesses.fix: On-chain chip governance before real value is at stake

weaknesses.what: Cohorts are filled by real members first; scripted members — real wallets under the same contract rules, whose forfeits fund real prizes and whose completed days are **not camera-verified** — top a cohort up only to a minimum (20 members in a 7-day cohort, 12 in a 21-day one)
weaknesses.why: A cohort must never be empty when someone installs the app during judging
weaknesses.fix: Disclosed here, in the app, in the demo video and in the pitch deck; their addresses are published in the build and every scripted member is labelled wherever it appears

weaknesses.what: A wallet is required before anything, even the Daily 25
weaknesses.why: One identity from the first tap; guest mode was considered and dropped
weaknesses.fix: The connect screen plays the recorded walkthrough without a wallet, so judges who cannot connect one still see the whole product

weaknesses.what: The full cycle is shown as a recorded walkthrough in the app, for judges
weaknesses.why: A judge can't wait 7 days
weaknesses.fix: It is a recording of the real app against the real devnet contract, taken from the first judged cohort. Members get a three-card tour instead

weaknesses.what: The faucet's fee sponsor key ships inside the app
weaknesses.why: A wallet with zero SOL cannot pay for its own first transaction, and there is no server to sign for it
weaknesses.fix: Anyone can extract the key, and empty the 0.05 SOL float it holds, so the contract bounds that instead of assuming it will not happen: one claim per wallet a day, a single daily budget of 0.72 SOL covering **every** lamport that leaves the faucet — top-ups and reimbursements alike — and a permissionless refill, so a drained sponsor is restored by the next crank pass rather than ending onboarding. Real fix: no faucet on mainnet, or a rate-limited relayer

weaknesses.what: The program keeps its upgrade authority during judging
weaknesses.why: A defect found while cohort #3 holds real test stakes must be fixable
weaknesses.fix: Used only for defect fixes that change no existing cohort, account layout or fund movement. Real fix: revoke the authority once the contract is final

weaknesses.what: A cohort nobody finished cannot settle until its league has a lobby open for joining
weaknesses.why: The carry-over has to go into a cohort members can still join, and the contract will not let a caller's timing decide otherwise: settlement is refused while no such cohort exists (error 6047). Opening the league's next cohort is permissionless and already due, and the crank does it before settling anything, so the refusal costs one automation pass
weaknesses.fix: Ship `deliver_carry_over` (Phase 2, already specified) so a league that stops opening cohorts entirely can still move the amount it would then hold

weaknesses.what: A Daily 25 done before the phone has ever read chain time is dated afterwards, from the phone's own uptime clock
weaknesses.why: The Daily 25 needs no connection, but a day is chain time (05:00 UTC), never the phone's clock. The last chain reading is kept, so this only happens after a reboot with no network since. Several such sittings are dated together, from the latest one's start; reps done offline across a reboot stay undated
weaknesses.fix: Keep one record per offline sitting and date each separately

weaknesses.what: Reminders are on-device only — no push
weaknesses.why: No server knows anyone's deadlines. The phone schedules a reminder when a Holdout starts and before each day's deadline (FR-068), from chain time; Android may deliver it a few minutes late, not at all after a restart until the app is opened, and never if notifications are declined. The deadline is the chain's, never the reminder's
weaknesses.fix: A push service fed by the chain, alongside the on-device reminders
